skill.name: configuring-dapr-pubsub
skill.description: Configure Dapr pub/sub components for Kafka or Redis, define subscriptions, publish events, integrate sidecars, deploy to Kubernetes, and troubleshoot event delivery.
skill.summary: Build Dapr pub/sub configurations and application patterns for event-driven services.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: All 51 static detections are false positives. The command alerts are Markdown examples, and the network references target a local Dapr sidecar. Semantic review found insecure production Kafka defaults and unpinned container images.

remediation.issue: Production guidance disables authentication, and the quick start disables TLS.
remediation.suggestion: Make TLS and SASL authentication the production default. Label unauthenticated settings as isolated local development examples.

remediation.issue: Deployment examples use mutable latest image tags.
remediation.suggestion: Pin application, Dapr, and Kafka images to reviewed versions or immutable digests.

semantic_findings.title: Insecure Kafka Defaults Presented for Production
semantic_findings.description: The quick start disables TLS, and the production Kafka example uses no authentication. Reuse can expose event data and permit unauthorized broker access.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited configuration explicitly sets disableTls to true and labels an authType none example as production guidance.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Container Images
semantic_findings.description: Deployment examples use latest image tags for application, Dapr, and Kafka containers. Mutable tags can introduce unreviewed or incompatible images during deployment.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Each cited deployment line uses a mutable latest tag, so image contents can change without a manifest update.

content.user_title: Configure Dapr Pub/Sub for Kafka and Redis
content.value_statement: Dapr pub/sub setup can fail when components, subscriptions, sidecars, and routes do not align. This skill provides practical Kafka and Redis patterns for local and Kubernetes deployments.
actual_capabilities: Drafts Dapr component manifests for Kafka and Redis backends.
Defines declarative and FastAPI programmatic subscriptions.
Shows event publishing through the local Dapr HTTP API.
Configures Kubernetes deployments with Dapr sidecar annotations and component scopes.
Provides local CLI and troubleshooting patterns for event delivery.
limitations: Examples require environment-specific broker addresses, ports, topics, and application identifiers.
The skill does not provision Kafka, Redis, Kubernetes, or Dapr installations.
It does not cover direct Kafka clients or non-Dapr messaging systems.
Production authentication, TLS, authorization, and image versions require independent review.

use_cases.title: Prototype Local Event Flows
use_cases.description: Create Redis or Kafka components, start Dapr sidecars, and test publishing between local services.

use_cases.title: Deploy Kubernetes Microservices
use_cases.description: Prepare component scopes, sidecar annotations, subscriptions, and deployment settings for a Kubernetes environment.

use_cases.title: Connect Specialized Agents
use_cases.description: Design topic routes for a triage service and specialist services using Dapr pub/sub.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Local Redis Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Dapr Redis pub/sub component for local development. Include one declarative subscription and list the values I must customize.

prompt_templates.title: Add FastAPI Publishing
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how my FastAPI service can publish order-created events through a local Dapr sidecar. Include error handling and a matching subscription route.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Secure Kafka Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Kubernetes Dapr Kafka component using TLS, SASL, secret references, and application scopes. Explain required broker and consumer settings.

prompt_templates.title: Design Multi-Service Routing
prompt_templates.prompt: Design Dapr topics and subscriptions for a triage service and three specialist services. Include CloudEvent fields, retry considerations, observability, and a verification plan.

output_examples.input: Create a secure Kafka component for the payments and ledger services.
output: A component plan uses TLS, SASL authentication, and Kubernetes secret references.
Scopes limit access to the payments and ledger application identifiers.
A checklist identifies broker addresses, consumer groups, and secret names that require customization.

output_examples.input: Troubleshoot why my inventory service receives no stock-updated events.
output: Verify that the pub/sub component name matches the subscription.
Compare the topic, route, application identifier, scope, and resource path.
Inspect Dapr sidecar metadata and logs, then publish a controlled test event.

output_examples.input: Plan event routing from a support triage service to specialist services.
output: Separate topics route concept, debugging, and response events.
Each specialist subscribes only to its required topic.
CloudEvent identifiers and session fields support tracing and response correlation.

best_practices: Use TLS, authentication, secret references, and application scopes for production brokers.
Keep component names, topics, routes, scopes, and application identifiers consistent.
Verify sidecar registration and event flow with controlled test messages before deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not reuse unauthenticated or TLS-disabled examples in production.
Do not expose broker credentials directly in component manifests.
Do not deploy mutable latest image tags in controlled environments.

faq.question: Does this skill install Dapr, Kafka, or Redis?
faq.answer: No. It provides configuration and integration guidance for existing environments.

faq.question: Can I use declarative subscriptions?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill covers Dapr subscription manifests with topics, routes, and application scopes.

faq.question: Does it support FastAPI services?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes programmatic subscription handlers and publishing through the Dapr HTTP API.

faq.question: Is the Kafka configuration production-ready?
faq.answer: Not without review. Production deployments need TLS, authentication, secret management, authorization, and pinned image versions.

faq.question: Can it configure direct Kafka clients?
faq.answer: No. The guidance uses Dapr pub/sub abstractions instead of direct broker clients.

faq.question: How does it help with troubleshooting?
faq.answer: It checks sidecar metadata, logs, component registration, topic routes, consumer groups, and test event delivery.
